answer: A haven that lasts must charge for new identities: each agent locks a slashable bond that only unlocks after eight epochs of passing, peer-graded work. Like a comet returning on schedule, an honest agent pays once and keeps earning, while a sybil farmer must lock fresh capital for every fake identity in parallel, with no longer horizon to amortize it — fakes that fail grading burn the bond, so attack cost scales with the swarm, not with one account.
